summary:
Wayfarer is a web-based single player game where you can explore Mars via space missions in different difficulty levels, providing a deeper enhancement of how missions in space are conducted in different roles, including a pilot, scientist, engineer, and a communications member. 

Space missions are generally conducted in the space and planets. Our game is inspired by the Artemis Program: We launched into the space, entered the orbital of Mars, followed by a landing of both an unmanned and manned spacecraft and conduction of scientific experiments. Lastly, we successfully re-entered the atmosphere and landed on Earth.

This game provides a realistic view of the Artemis Program through simulated missions for both the ones who are unfamiliar with the concept and those who already have the related background, in an interactive and enjoyable way with random events occurring throughout the mission that should be prevented or recovered.
details:
Wayfarer simulates the most current space missions by the launching into the Space, entering the orbital of Mars, followed by a landing of both unmanned and manned spacecraft and conduction of scientific experiments, lastly successfully re-entering the atmosphere and landing on Earth. Our scientific experiment include a microscope, centrifigure, growth chamber, and an insulin pen observatery.

Our project is not based on virtual steps of any space mission, which creates a significant difference. The stages of our game is inspired from the Artemis Program, mentioned above, and our scientific experiments have the same order of the real ones implemented as used in our resource.

Our desired impact is to teach and demonstrate how space missions are conducted in different roles by giving examples of solid active operations, which will help to show how space is going to shape. Thus, our long-term impact will be to raise awareness upon the topic

We used html on VisualStudio as it is both practical and provides and easy way to collaborate between our coding members.

Our vision while planning the game was it to be educating while not boring the player with heavy data. Thus, we managed to include real experiments, steps of space missions, and landing and re-enterings with steps simulated by Artemis, while keeping the player on the screen with the help of random events such as thermal buildups, space debris, loss of signal, and crosswinds during launchs.

We thought that our game must entertain both beginners and people who are familiar to space and relevant topics. Thus, we made our game as realistic as possible. Yet, we considered that a game that is too realistic will bore the player after a short time. Thus, we came up with the idea of random events, which makes the player remain on game while getting a wider understanding. During our planning of the game sceneario, we realised that if we use a wider variety of data and examples, our game will not be scientifically consistent. Thus, we used the official data specifically up-to-date in order to prevent misconceptions. Our team also considered that in order to be as educative as possible, we should add a variety of scenarios of different experiments, landings, launches, and surface missions. Thus, we completed our game with the latest version.
